characters.why: Listing: 'firm, wise and naturally conversational', 'quiet confidence without being cold', 'tells you the truth without making it harsh'. That fits Kiran's flat, blunt register and her rule that under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill. It is a conversation voice, not a narrator, ad or helpline read. It is also the only young female shortlist voice whose listing names English-speaking audiences, which matters because the lead carries the English cut. Preview measured median about 239 Hz (10th to 90th percentile 190 to 348 Hz, about 10 semitones of movement). That leaves room for the 'Sneha' register to sit a little higher and softer. Open risks for the listening test: the listing says nothing about small-city Madhya Pradesh colour; the switch between 'Sneha' and Kiran has to come from tags alone, and a listing cannot show whether it will; it is about 3 semitones above Mausi's first choice, so the two women in one room is the main pair check.
characters.backup_why: Replaces Apsara (QpSjVAs2VI5btKzupPaD), which is Series 2's lead (nandini in content/series2/cast.json) and may not be used in Series 1. Found by creative_list_voices on 26 Nov 2026 (languages hi, female, young, search 'conversational Hinglish'). Listing: 'warm, friendly female Indian voice, natural Hindi and Hinglish narration with clear English pronunciation, conversational storytelling tone'. It is the only young female Hindi listing in that search that names English pronunciation, which matters because the lead carries the English cut. Preview measured (same method as casting/review.json) median 276 Hz, 235 to 333 Hz, 6.0 semitones, voiced 0.95. Not used in Series 2 or either proof cast (grep of content/, 26 Nov). Risks: it is sold for narration and wellness, so it may come out soft and polished rather than blunt; previews mispredicted the cast voices by 2 to 3 semitones (Yashvi preview 239 Hz, takes about 214; Savitri preview 200, takes about 235), so its pairing with Chhoti (takes 308 Hz) and Mausi must be rechecked on its own takes. Untested on any line.

casting_review.verdict: Keep Yashvi G. No clear failure on words, spoken tags or partner separation; one tag over-read (kiran_t3 whispered), which plan 7.8 fixes with a simpler tag before any voice change. Provisional on three ear checks: kiran_t3, the Sneha-to-Kiran switch, and the Mausi pair.
evidence: Words: all four transcripts match the script. kiran_t1 'आप जाग रहे हैं, मैं तो बस आपके दूद में केसर डाल रही थी' (केसर clear). kiran_t2 'पूलीस हो? नहीं? तो फिर चाहिये क्या तुमें?' ('Police' heard; the -l en pass also gives 'Police? No?'). kiran_t3 'Mossy, the milk has split.' kiran_t4 'You want the one with the burnt wrist? Reika. She doesn't do weddings anymore.' (word pass: 'Rika').
Spoken tags: none in any transcript.

kiran_t3 [quietly] came out whispered by every measure: voiced ratio 0.23 against 0.74 to 0.88 on her other takes, spectral flatness 0.091 (highest of all 24 takes; her others 0.030 to 0.048) and centroid 3,746 Hz (her others 1,664 to 2,190). Level -33.3 dB, 11 to 12 dB under her plain lines. The words survive in transcription, but the check asks for 'quiet but fully voiced'. The ellipsis gives a 0.42 s pause, which passes.

The same [quietly] inside kiran_t2 was obeyed as intended: the second half drops 6 to 7 dB (-19.3/-20.3 to -27.4/-25.0 dB) and stays voiced (0.87 to 0.88). So the whisper is a tag reading on one short English line, not a voice that cannot do quiet.

Sneha against Kiran (kiran_t1 vs kiran_t2): Sneha is not higher (median 222 against 216 Hz, 0.5 semitone) and not softer (-22.7 against -22.3 dB). What does differ: kiran_t1 has five short hesitation pauses (0.15 to 0.28 s) and a narrower range (7.0 against 10.3 semitones). By measure the switch rests on hesitation alone; whether it reads as one woman dropping an act needs the ear.
kiran_t4: 0.43 s pause after 'wrist?' before 'Rekha'. That is a sentence boundary, not clearly a hesitation. 'Rekha' transcribed 'Reika'/'Rika' twice: the aspirated kh may be soft. Ear check.
Indian English: not decidable from a transcript. 'Mausi' comes out 'Mossy' (an English-model spelling); 'doesn't', 'anymore' read normally.
casting_review.production_direction: No [low voice] for Kiran, and no quiet-family tag on any of her retakes (D-022); first takes keep the script text. Quiet lines go out with [calm] or as the bare line, with the level set in the mix. Her retakes follow D-022 rule 1: the script text with every quiet-family tag deleted, [calm] only if no tag is left, then the bare line. The locked alarm line's next take is '[calm] Mausi... the milk has split.', then the bare line 'Mausi... the milk has split.'; check voiced_ratio is 0.6 or more.
casting_review.switch_if: Switch to Rudrika (2kb0BzqPNMYVxWCj9dqt) only if the owner's ear finds the Sneha and Kiran takes sound like two actors or the same read, or the English drifts American or British. By measure (D-022 rule 4), a switch is tested only if Kiran's final take is still under 0.6 voiced after the [calm] and bare rungs on 3 or more voice-wanted lines, across at least 2 episodes, while at least half of the other Series 1 voices' quiet-free retakes pass. If that is met, S10 runs Rudrika's four casting lines (about 300 credits, with kiran_t3 as '[calm] Mausi... the milk has split.') and the Chhoti and Mausi pair checks, and the result goes back to the Arbiter before anything is re-voiced. A whispered [low voice] take is no longer a trigger.

d022.production_direction_before: Do not tag Kiran's must-be-heard English lines [quietly]. For the locked alarm line use '[low voice] Mausi... the milk has split.' or no tag with the level set in the mix. Retake kiran_t3 that way when the episode is voiced and check voiced_ratio is 0.6 or more.
d022.switch_if_before: Switch to Rudrika only if the ear finds the Sneha and Kiran takes sound like two actors or the same read, or the English drifts American or British, or a [low voice] retake of kiran_t3 also comes out whispered.

characters.voice_name: Amit Wadhwa - Friendly and Conversational Voice
characters.why: Listing: a bilingual English and Hindi voice-over artist with a 'calm, friendly and conversational tone'. Of all the male listings read, it gives the clearest promise that one voice reads both cuts, and Aditya's careful English is half his register in each language. Preview measured median about 126 Hz (110 to 176 Hz, about 8 semitones), in light-baritone range. Its 11-second preview gives the most reliable reading of any male shortlist voice. A calm, courteous base suits a man who 'reads out a prescription' and whose calm is the threat. Open risks for the listening test: it is an ad and e-learning voice and may come out polished or announcer-like rather than soft-spoken; the listing has no small-city colour; whether the voice catches on 'मोहित' without turning theatrical is untested.
characters.backup_why: Listing: warm deep male, 'conversational, articulate', 'clear diction, measured pacing', 'natural Hindi-English conversation'. That matches the English nouns of his trade (dose, sedative, SIM) inside Hindi lines and his unhurried pace. Preview median about 168 Hz, but the clip is only 3.5 s, so the figure is shaky. It is the backup because it names Hinglish rather than English. Switch to it first if Amit Wadhwa reads as an ad voice or too bright on the menace lines.

characters.why: Listing: 'a mature Indian female voice with a gentle Bihari inflection', 'warm, unhurried tone', 'rich, motherly quality', for 'regional storytelling' that calls for 'cultural texture'. Mature, motherly, unhurried and regional is the nearest any listing came to a 56-year-old Bundelkhand-side marriage broker. A Hindi-heartland inflection suits her better than standard broadcast Hindi, though Bihari is not Bundeli. Preview measured median about 200 Hz with a narrow spread (168 to 222 Hz, about 5 semitones), matching her rule that she never raises her voice. Its periodicity score (0.84) was rougher than the smoother motherly voices (0.92), a weak hint of grain. Open risks for the listening test: nothing promises a laugh or a paan-chewer's mouth; the listing says nothing about English; at about 3 semitones below Kiran's first choice, the two women must still be easy to tell apart with eyes closed.

casting_review.verdict: Keep Savitri for now. Words, tags and full voicing pass. The open problem is the pair with Kiran: in the takes Mausi sits 1 to 2.4 semitones above Kiran, the reverse of the previews, with near-equal brightness in Hindi. That is close, not proven indistinguishable, so it goes to the ear first.
evidence: Words: mausi_t1 'खाना खाया तुने? जूट मत बोल बाख की साइट वाली जेब में मतरी रख़ी है' ('Bag' and 'side' heard; -l en pass 'in the bag's side pocket'). mausi_t2 'अचा सुन, दामाजीने दूट पीलिया, भीटा?'. mausi_t3 'Listen, did Damajji drink his milk, beta?'. mausi_t4 word for word. 'दामाद जी' is heard as 'दामाजी' in both languages: the final द runs into जी. Ear check, likely natural.
Spoken tags: none, including [laughs].

Fully voiced on the code question, as the bible requires: voiced 0.83 (mausi_t2) and 0.87 (mausi_t3); her lowest is 0.76. Ellipsis pauses are real: 0.43 s after 'सुन' (two short gaps) and 0.36 s after 'Listen'.
mausi_t4 [gently][slowly] is 2.7 dB softer than mausi_t3 and lower (195 against 235 Hz), with a 0.51 s pause between sentences. Slower is not shown by chars/s (16.0 against 15.1, different texts).
[laughs] in mausi_t1: no separate non-word segment between 'तूने?' and 'झूठ' (only a 0.39 s gap); whisper stretches 'बोल' to about 1 s. Whether a laugh happened cannot be told by measure.
Pitch: 235, 242, 235 and 195 Hz (preview was 200). For a 56-year-old 'warm, low, grainy' voice this is higher than planned, and [warmly] seems to lift her ([gently] gave 195).

Pair with Kiran: kiran_t1/mausi_t1 222 against 235 Hz (1.0 semitone), kiran_t2/mausi_t2 216 against 242 (2.0), kiran_t3/mausi_t3 211 against 235 (1.9, Kiran's figure weak because that take is whispered), kiran_t4/mausi_t3 205 against 235 (2.4). Centroid in Hindi: Kiran 2,190/2,056 Hz, Mausi 2,139/2,085 Hz.
Pair with Billu: billu_t3/mausi_t3 150 against 235 Hz (7.8 semitones), billu_t1/mausi_t1 174 against 235 (5.2). Clearly apart.
casting_review.production_direction: Try [gently] or no tag before [warmly] on her phone lines; in this test [warmly] went with the higher pitch.
casting_review.switch_if: If the ear cannot tell Kiran and Mausi apart with eyes closed (kiran_t2 against mausi_t2, kiran_t4 against mausi_t3), switch Mausi, not Kiran, to Kahani G (ZthnDvLLxYzM9qeFVSJe), because Mausi is the one off her brief in pitch. Re-test mausi_t1 to t4 (about 265 credits at this test's rate) and recheck both pairs. Note Kahani G is also Series 2's door2_woman backup.

Can I sleep?' exact. chhoti_t4 'DB, it's only one night, isn't it?': 'Didi' heard as 'DB'. Ear check, likely the model's spelling.
Spoken tags: none; no 'giggles' word.

[giggles]: no separate segment. The first word is stretched in both takes (whisper puts 'मौसी' at 0.05 to 1.90 s in chhoti_t1 and 'Maasi' at 0.05 to 1.04 s in chhoti_t3), consistent with a giggle folded into it. Not provable by measure.

[nervous][small voice] obeyed: chhoti_t2 and chhoti_t4 are 4 to 6 dB under the cheerful takes (-25.6/-26.7 against -21.6/-21.1 dB), lower (258/250 against 308 Hz) and narrower (5.9/7.9 against 11.0/11.5 semitones), still voiced (0.76/0.73) and fully transcribed.
Height: cheerful takes median 308 Hz, 90th percentile 444 Hz. That is the range where 'childish or shrill' would live; it is not a verdict.

Pairs: Chhoti to Kiran 5.7 semitones (cheerful) and 3.1 (small voice). Small-voice Chhoti to Mausi is 1.1 semitones (chhoti_t2 258 against mausi_t2 242 Hz); her frightened lines go to Kiran, so this is a note.
casting_review.switch_if: Switch to Shreya G (KawjuInLhxYsnVJlqveG) if the ear hears a child or shrillness on chhoti_t1 or chhoti_t3. Note Geet is also Series 2's reporter backup.

characters.why: Listing: middle-aged male, 'heavy serious'. Preview measured median about 178 Hz with one of the flattest spreads (167 to 212 Hz, about 4 semitones) and the darkest timbre of any voice sampled. That suits a tired clerk who says two or three words at a time and has written a thousand names. The pitch matters most: at the chowki he speaks beside Aditya, and he sits about 6 semitones above Aditya's first choice and 2.7 below Billu's. Open risks for the listening test: the listing is two words and the preview only 3 s; the very dark timbre may be a dull recording rather than the voice; one- and two-word lines are where v4 is least stable; nothing is said about English.
characters.backup_why: Listing: middle-aged male, Haryanvi accent label, 'News reporter'. Its preview was the flattest male clip measured (about 3.4 semitones), which fits 'flat and tired'. A north Indian regional label suits a small police post. It is the backup because it sits only about 1.7 semitones above Aditya's first choice (139 against 126 Hz), so the chowki scene risks two similar men. Switch to it if ajay singh sounds muffled or menacing. If Aditya also moves to his backup (Arjun, about 168 Hz), recheck this pair by ear.

casting_evidence.browsed: Hindi listing (languages ["hi"], page_size 30): two unfiltered pages (60 entries). Then filtered searches: female + middle_aged (two pages), female + old, female + husky / deep / raspy / mature / serious / confident / sassy, male + old. Then text searches: 'Hinglish', 'English', 'aunty', 'web series', 'dadi'. The female + old and male + old searches ran out of Hindi voices and returned other languages; those were ignored. The search 'aunty mother drama character' returned nothing.
casting_evidence.english: The listing has no field for a second language. English appears only in free-text descriptions. Of the twelve first choices and backups, these name English or Hinglish: Yashvi G (Hindi and English audiences), Apsara (Hinglish), Amit Wadhwa (bilingual English and Hindi), Arjun (Hindi-English), Shreya G (Hinglish). Mausi, Billu, Chhoti and the constable have no first choice that names English; no listing that did also fitted those roles. Some speakers have a separate voice_id labelled en-indian (several 'Bunty' entries), but the English cut must use the same voice_id, so those were not used.
casting_evidence.preview_measurement: 38 public preview clips (one per voice) were downloaded to the session scratchpad and measured with a simple autocorrelation pitch tracker: median pitch, 10th to 90th percentile spread, a periodicity score as a rough smoothness proxy, and spectral centroid as a rough brightness proxy. The clips differ in text, length (3 to 14 s) and acting style, so the numbers are indicative only. Clips of 3 to 4 s (Arjun, ajay singh, Ramniwas, Amit Ratan, Nazir Qureshi) are the least reliable. The numbers were used to keep each pair apart and to rule out high or shouted voices. They say nothing about tag obedience, accent or English.
casting_evidence.library_voices: All twelve first choices and backups are listed as library voices (is_library_voice true), not voices already in the workspace. Whether creative_generate_speech accepts a library voice_id directly, or needs it added to a voice slot first (the plan records 160 slots on Pro), was not checked, because no speech was generated.
casting_evidence.not_verified: No take was heard or generated. Not verified: obedience to [laughs], [giggles], [whispers], [small voice], [flatly], [teasing] and the other tags on eleven_v4 for any of these voices; Indian English accent for any voice; the 'Sneha' to Kiran register switch inside one voice; Bundelkhand or Madhya Pradesh colour for anyone; whether Chhoti reads 19 and not younger; whether the constable's one-word lines are stable.

how_to_run: Create one flow for the series casting test with creative_create_flow and pass its flow_id to every call.

One creative_generate_speech call per test line: prompt = text exactly as written (tags included), model_id eleven_v4, voice_id = the character's voice_id, generations_count 1. Never re-call to retry a pending result.

Download each take at once and check duration with ffprobe. Record it in content/series1/voice/casting-test.jsonl with {line_id, lang, voice_id, model, text, generation_id, credits, file, duration_s, status}.

Judge each take on its checks, transcribe it to confirm the words (including the Latin-script words inside Hindi lines), then run the pair checks by ear: kiran_t3 against mausi_t3, billu_t3 against mausi_t3, aditya_t4 against constable_t4.
A character whose first choice fails a reject_if item is re-tested on the backup with the same lines. When all six pass, set status to "cast".
listening_test.estimated_cost: 24 lines, 1,395 characters including tags (Python len). At the measured ~1.25 credits a character (skill note), that is about 1,750 credits for one pass. A backup re-test of one character's four lines adds about 300.
reject_if: A voice ignores its tags or speaks a tag aloud.
English lines come out American or British.
Kiran's 'Sneha' and Kiran lines sound like two different actors, or no different at all.
Mausi's code question (mausi_t2, mausi_t3) comes out whispered, cold or villainous.
Kiran and Mausi, or Billu and Mausi, are hard to tell apart with eyes closed.
Aditya raises his voice or sounds theatrical on aditya_t2, or he and the constable are hard to tell apart.
Chhoti sounds like a child or goes shrill.
The constable's one-word lines clip, stretch or add syllables.

casting_test.credit_rate_note: 1,395 credits for 1,395 characters including tags: about 1.0 credit a character on this test, not the skill's 1.25.
casting_test.transcript_source: local whisper.cpp (whisper-cli 'ggml-small.bin', no prompt, script not given). 'transcript' = forced to the take's language; 'transcript_autodetect' = -l auto; 'transcript_en_pass' (Hindi takes) = -l en, which mostly translates rather than transliterates, so it only shows whether Latin-script words were heard. Connector transcription not used (its text cannot be read back).

ear_check.listen_for: Whispered or quiet-but-voiced? Measures say whispered (voiced 0.23, flatness 0.091). The locked alarm line; Mausi must hear it on a call.
Same woman dropping an act? Measures show hesitation pauses in t1 but no higher or softer 'Sneha' (0.5 semitone, 0.4 dB apart).
Kiran and Mausi apart with eyes closed? 1.0 to 2.4 semitones apart, Mausi the higher, similar brightness in Hindi. If not, Mausi goes to Kahani G.
An added sigh or syllable before or inside 'नाम?' (two voiced parts, 0.28 s gap). Also whether 'नाम' and 'पूरा नाम' (constable_t2) are said right.
Squeal or crack on the loud line (281 Hz median, about 8 to 11 semitones above his other takes).
Reads 19, not a child; not shrill (top about 444 Hz); a giggle is actually there.
Is there a laugh? Warm and grainy, not rustic comedy? 'दामाद जी' also heard as 'दामाजी' in mausi_t2/t3.
'Rekha' said the Hindi way (transcribed 'Reika'/'Rika'); is the 0.43 s beat before it a hesitation?
Catch on 'मोहित' only; last sentence soft but not breathy; Aditya clearly unlike the constable (measured 6.6 semitones apart).
Indian English, no American or British drift, one take per character. A transcript cannot show accent.
